```{r}
#| include: false
source("_setup.R")
```

The global Moran's I says the map is clustered. **Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA)**, here **local Moran's I**, say **where**: they give each area its own statistic, test and cluster type.

## One statistic per area

```{r}
loc <- localmoran(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)
head(round(loc, 3))
```

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Ii` | local Moran's I of this area (positive: similar to its neighbours; negative: unlike them) |
| `E.Ii`, `Var.Ii` | its expectation and variance with no pattern |
| `Z.Ii` | z-score |
| `Pr(z != E(Ii))` | two-sided p-value |

The **sum of the local values divided by the sum of the weights equals the global I**: the global statistic is the average of the local ones.

```{r}
c(global = unname(moran.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate[1]),
  mean_local = mean(loc[, "Ii"])) |> round(3)
```

## Cluster types from the quadrants

Combine the **quadrant** from the Moran scatterplot with **significance**:

```{r}
z <- as.numeric(scale(blocks$dengue_per_100k)); lag_z <- lag.listw(lw, z, zero.policy = TRUE)
p <- loc[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"]
blocks$lisa <- case_when(
  p >= 0.05 ~ "Not significant",
  z > 0 & lag_z > 0 ~ "High-High (hot spot)",
  z < 0 & lag_z < 0 ~ "Low-Low (cold spot)",
  z > 0 & lag_z < 0 ~ "High-Low (outlier)",
  TRUE ~ "Low-High (outlier)")
blocks$lisa <- factor(blocks$lisa, levels = c("High-High (hot spot)", "Low-Low (cold spot)", "High-Low (outlier)", "Low-High (outlier)", "Not significant"))
table(blocks$lisa)
```

```{r}
cols <- c("High-High (hot spot)" = "#d7191c", "Low-Low (cold spot)" = "#2c7bb6", "High-Low (outlier)" = "#fdae61", "Low-High (outlier)" = "#abd9e9", "Not significant" = "grey90")
ggplot(blocks) + geom_sf(aes(fill = lisa), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) + scale_fill_manual(values = cols, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "LISA cluster map of dengue incidence", subtitle = "p < 0.05, unadjusted, queen weights") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

In this synthetic district the generator planted a **hot spot in the south-east**, a **cold spot in the north-west** and **one high block inside the cold area**. The map should show all three: the red group, the blue group, and an orange *High-Low* outlier.

## Multiple testing

You just ran **79 tests**. At 5% about 4 areas appear "significant" by chance alone, and the tests are **correlated** because neighbouring areas share neighbours. Adjust the p-values with `p.adjust()` or be cautious:

```{r}
p_fdr <- p.adjust(p, method = "fdr")                 # adjust the 79 p-values (Benjamini-Hochberg)
c(unadjusted_p_lt_05 = sum(p < 0.05), fdr_adjusted_p_lt_05 = sum(p_fdr < 0.05), bonferroni_p_lt_05 = sum(p.adjust(p, "bonferroni") < 0.05))
```

-   `"bonferroni"` is the most conservative, `"fdr"` (Benjamini-Hochberg) controls the false discovery rate and is a sensible default.
-   Treat LISA as **exploratory**: it shows where to look, not proof of a cluster in each area.

## A permutation version

The analytical p-values assume the data are close to normal. **Conditional permutation** shuffles the neighbours' values around each area, and works better for skewed rates:

```{r}
set.seed(3)
loc_perm <- localmoran_perm(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, nsim = 499, zero.policy = TRUE)
head(round(loc_perm, 3), 3)
c(analytic_sig = sum(p < 0.05), permutation_sig = sum(loc_perm[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"] < 0.05))
```

## Reading cluster maps

-   A **High-High** area has a high value **and** high-value neighbours: a hot spot, where to look for a shared cause or to target an intervention.
-   A **High-Low** area is a **spatial outlier**: unusually high among low neighbours (a local outbreak, a data problem, a special site). Check the record before interpreting.
-   The result depends on the **weights**, the **variable** (rates, not counts) and the **significance rule**. Say which you used.
-   Each area's cluster status uses its neighbours, so a hot spot typically covers several areas, not one.

## Take-home

-   Local Moran's I gives **a statistic and p-value per area**; the quadrant tells the cluster type (HH, LL, HL, LH).
-   You ran many tests: **adjust** (`"fdr"`) or treat the result as exploratory, and consider permutation p-values.
-   Pair the global test with the local map, and always report variable, weights and adjustment.
